lens: The week closed on a busier tape: Dream Finders agreed to buy Beazer Homes for ~$2.2B with four covered banks split across the sides, Apollo made a recommended ~£5.7B run at easyJet (Evercore for the airline, Barclays for Apollo), and argenx’s tender for Forte went live — a cross-sector burst of signings against a rebound in stocks and advisory names.

stories.headline: Dream Finders to acquire Beazer Homes for ~$2.2B; four covered banks split the sides
stories.why_it_matters: Dream Finders Homes (NYSE: DFH) entered a definitive agreement to acquire Beazer Homes (NYSE: BZH) in an all-cash deal at ~$2.2B enterprise value ($33.50/share), forming the nation’s sixth-largest homebuilder. The release names Goldman Sachs and BofA Securities as financial advisers to Dream Finders (buy-side, with Zelman and Vestra; Goldman and BofA also provide committed financing) and J.P. Morgan and Moelis & Company as Beazer’s financial advisers (sell-side). Expected to close Q4 2026 subject to a Beazer shareholder vote. A public-to-public homebuilder merger runs antitrust, financing and shareholder-documentation workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: This deal puts four covered desks on one transaction — engage Goldman/BofA (Dream Finders) and JPMorgan/Moelis (Beazer). A ~$2.2B public-company merger runs antitrust, committed-financing and proxy diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: Dream Finders/Beazer definitive agreement ($33.50/share, ~$2.2B)
Expected close (subject to Beazer shareholder vote)

stories.headline: Apollo makes a recommended ~£5.7B offer for easyJet; Evercore advises easyJet, Barclays advises Apollo
stories.why_it_matters: Apollo Global Management made a recommended acquisition offer for UK low-cost carrier easyJet plc (LSE: EZJ) valuing it at ~£5.7B, after rival bidder Castlelake stated it does not intend to make an offer. The Rule 2.7 announcement names Evercore as lead financial adviser to easyJet (with BNP Paribas as financial adviser & corporate broker) and Barclays as sole financial adviser to Apollo (which has a highly-confident letter on the debt financing). A cross-border, take-private of a listed airline runs UK Takeover Code, antitrust and financing-diligence workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Evercore (easyJet) and Barclays (Apollo) — a ~£5.7B cross-border airline take-private runs UK Takeover Code, antitrust and lender diligence a secure room organizes over a long path to close.

deal_clock.event: Apollo makes recommended ~£5.7B offer for easyJet; Castlelake steps aside

stories.headline: argenx’s tender offer for Forte Biosciences is live; Guggenheim advises Forte, Goldman advises argenx
stories.why_it_matters: Still fresh from Aug 6: argenx (via Avena Merger Sub) commenced its all-cash tender offer for all shares of Forte Biosciences (Nasdaq: FBRX), and Forte’s board filed its SC 14D-9 recommending shareholders tender — the ~$2.2B deal (announced Jul 27) is now a live filed tender. The filing names Guggenheim Securities as Forte’s financial adviser (fairness opinion) and Goldman Sachs as argenx’s adviser. A commenced tender runs a compressed confirmatory-diligence and close clock to the offer expiration.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Guggenheim (Forte) and Goldman (argenx) — a commenced tender offer runs a tight confirmatory-diligence and close timeline a secure room keeps organized through expiration.

deal_clock.event: argenx agrees to acquire Forte Biosciences (~$2.2B)
Tender offer commenced; Forte files SC 14D-9 recommending tender

stories.headline: Identiv files its definitive proxy for its asset sale; Raymond James is the company’s financial adviser
stories.why_it_matters: Identiv (Nasdaq: INVE) filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFM14A) for the sale of its purchased assets, moving the process from the July preliminary proxy to a shareholder vote. The filing names Raymond James as Identiv’s financial adviser (fairness opinion delivered Jun 24, 2026; sell-side). An asset-sale proxy runs disclosure and shareholder-approval workstreams to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Raymond James (Identiv) — an asset-sale heading to a shareholder vote runs disclosure and confirmatory workstreams a secure room organizes through the meeting.

deal_clock.event: Raymond James delivers fairness opinion to Identiv board
Definitive proxy (DEFM14A) filed

stories.headline: Prologis’ ~$18.8B recommended combination with SEGRO keeps seven covered banks in play
stories.why_it_matters: Still live: the Rule 2.7 announcement for Prologis’ ~£14.0B (~$18.8B) recommended all-share combination with UK logistics REIT SEGRO names advisers on both sides — seven are covered banks. SEGRO (sell-side): Evercore and Morgan Stanley (joint lead), Goldman Sachs, and UBS (corporate broker/adviser). Prologis (buy-side): J.P. Morgan (joint lead), BofA Securities and Citi (with Rothschild and Eastdil). A cross-border public-company REIT combination runs UK Takeover Code, antitrust and shareholder-documentation workstreams to a targeted 1H 2027 close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage the SEGRO advisers (Evercore, Morgan Stanley, Goldman, UBS) and Prologis advisers (JPMorgan, BofA, Citi) — a ~$18.8B cross-border REIT combination runs months of Takeover Code and antitrust diligence a secure room organizes.

deal_clock.event: Prologis/SEGRO recommended combination announced (~$18.8B)
Targeted completion

stories.headline: LivePerson heads into its Aug 20 vote on the SoundHound AI merger; Houlihan Lokey advises LivePerson
stories.why_it_matters: Still live ahead of the vote: LivePerson (Nasdaq: LPSN) filed further solicitation material (Form 425) ahead of its Aug 20 special meeting on its stock-for-stock merger with SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN). Houlihan Lokey Capital is LivePerson’s financial adviser and delivered the fairness opinion. Secured noteholders agreed to exchange ~$350M of par notes at a discount to enable common-stock consideration, so the vote carries real execution risk and runs heavy proxy-solicitation and disclosure workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Houlihan Lokey (LivePerson) — a debt-laden stock-for-stock merger heading to a knife-edge shareholder vote runs intensive proxy and disclosure workstreams a secure room supports through the Aug 20 meeting.

deal_clock.event: SoundHound AI agrees to acquire LivePerson (stock-for-stock)
LivePerson special meeting / shareholder vote

stories.headline: Stocks rebound to end the week — S&P +0.43%, Nasdaq +0.95% — as the VIX eases to ~14.9 and the 10Y slips to ~4.64%
stories.why_it_matters: Equities bounced back Friday morning after midweek softness: the S&P 500 rose +0.43% (~7,743) and the Nasdaq +0.95% (~26,600) on a renewed megacap-tech bid, with the Dow +0.23% (~54,010). The VIX eased to ~14.9 and the 10Y Treasury slipped to ~4.64%. Advisory names were broadly higher (LAZ +1.8%, GS +0.7%, MS +0.5%, EVR +0.4%) as two fresh multi-bank M&A signings — Dream Finders/Beazer and Apollo/easyJet — landed on the tape. A firm, low-volatility close is the backdrop dealmakers want for launching and progressing processes.
stories.suggested_action: Use the calm, risk-on close to keep the conversation on execution — a supportive tape is when boards greenlight and advance processes, and room readiness protects the timeline.

talking_point.quote: The week ended with real signings, not just filings: Dream Finders/Beazer put four of the banks we cover on one $2.2B deal, and Apollo’s recommended run at easyJet added a cross-border take-private with Evercore and Barclays. Both are exactly the multi-party, cross-border processes where secure room readiness sets the execution pace. As you head into the weekend, which of your live mandates most needs its diligence environment locked before the next milestone?

talking_point.context: Pairs a risk-on Friday with two fresh multi-bank signings — a natural, upbeat way to open an execution-certainty conversation into the weekend.

items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed receipt of proposals, but no firm offer, price, or adviser roster disclosed — an early-stage UK Takeover Code situation, not a mandate.

items.company: GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) — Patient Care Solutions
items.lead: On its Q2 call, CEO Peter Arduini confirmed a formal review of strategic options for the Patient Care Solutions segment, explicitly including “a sale and other value-enhancing transactions.” Segment Q2 revenue was $675M, down 13.3%.
items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed that a review is underway — but whether it sells, at what price, to whom, with which adviser, and on what timeline are all unconfirmed. A potential carve-out mandate, not a rumored deal.
